newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda 1st qtr coffee earnings rise to $95.2 mln.
newsitem.headline: Uganda 1st qtr coffee earnings rise to $95.2 mln.

text.p: Coffee exports earned Uganda $95.2 million in the first quarter of 1996/97 (October-December) compared to $88.1 million in the same period the previous season, the Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) said.
UCDA put exports in the quarter at 1,290,986 60-kg bags from 795,502 bags a year earlier, the highest quarterly figures for four years.
The high volume was attributed to a good crop in the major coffee growing areas of Eastern and Central Uganda which were in their peak season.
Targeted procurement of 986,793 60-kg bags was superceded by 38.2 percent, reaching 1,363,610 bags. Exports also exceeded their target of 935,901 bags and $91.3 million.
The level of arabicas procured increased to 120,646 bags from 114,653 a year before, but was still below the record 271,657 bags achieved in 1994/95.
Robustas rose to 1,242,878 bags from 662,322 in the 1995/96 first quarter.
Procurement by private exporters rose by 23.7 percent to 1,310,786 bags from 1,059,437 as their liquidity position strengthened.
Private exporter activity rose to 1,254,478 bags worth $91.4 million as opposed to 737,793 bags worth $80.3 million in the same quarter of 1995/96, the report said.
Local coffee prices moved in line with international prices. Prices for fair average quality (FAQ) ranged between 700 and 900 shillings per kg while Kiboko ranged between 350 and 400 per kg.
Arabica parchment prices oscillated around 1,150 to 1,250 shillings a kg during the first quarter of 1996/97.

Average farmgate prices for the quarter stood at 833.3, 783.3 and 733.3 shillings per kg in October, November and December 1996 respectively versus 1,224, 1,262 and 1,080 shillings in the same months of 1995.
